g_policy.reason: The banner is opt-in and its offer copy states the 30-minute reward before play. The decline and ad-failure fields leave the app unchanged.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is a 30-minute in-app break from sponsored cards, not cash or a transferable item.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger uses an article-open counter and a return to the home feed, not chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The adds and decline fields leave free reading, saving, and sharing available; the reward temporarily hides ads.

g_brand_safety.reason: The placement is a banner on s01 Home · Top Stories, which is rated content safe, above the first story.

c1_revealed_value.reason: As a product change, the reward gives the player a cleaner experience in the observed read-a-story flow f01 and category-browsing flow f02.

c2_evidence.reason: The what-makes-it-work field claims AOL shows a full-screen video ad after every third article, which no product-model element supports. The subscribers field also treats every reader as free merely because no paid plan was observed, and the rationale calls the ad placements cheap without evidence.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward expires after 30 minutes and does not grant lasting paid access or take an advantage from other users or creators.

c5_moment.reason: The trigger places the offer on the home feed after the reader returns from an article, rather than interrupting an article.

c6_fits_simula.reason: The flow uses a sponsored game and grants the reward only once play is confirmed; an unconfirmed play leaves the feed unchanged.

c7_specific.reason: The idea names the s01 home feed, its category pills, and the sponsored cards observed at s01.e44 and s02.e13.

other_concern: The reward says its 30-minute timer starts when the game ends, but access waits for play confirmation; a verification delay could shorten the usable break.
